title: The Oracle Problem in Software Testing: A Survey
locator: PDF pp.1–2 introduction and oracle classification; follow-up section fetches timed out
claim: Input generation does not supply expected behavior; partial automated oracles and human domain information remain relevant.
context: Survey of oracle approaches, 2015 author manuscript.
limitations: Not all surveyed papers inspected; introduction supports problem framing, not comparative effectiveness.

title: QuickCheck: A Lightweight Tool for Random Testing of Haskell Programs
evidence_type: original tool paper and case studies
claim: Generated cases need meaningful distributions and correct properties; the unification example exposes trivial accepted cases and an invalid specification.
context: Haskell property testing and authors' applications.
limitations: Case studies rather than controlled general effectiveness estimates; generation/specification effort can be substantial.

title: Are Mutants a Valid Substitute for Real Faults in Software Testing?
claim: Mutation detection correlates with real-fault detection after coverage controls, with unsupported fault classes and sampling limits.
context: 357 real faults in five well-tested Java programs, developer and generated tests.
limitations: Bug/commit-link selection bias; program/language and operator scope constrain transfer.

title: Reducing Failure-Inducing Inputs
locator: ddmin implementation, generic_test and expected_exc; 1-minimal explanation; reduction of code preserving normal functionality
claim: Reduction requires an appropriate same-failure predicate; 1-minimal results are relative to reduction units and validity constraints.
context: Worked Python examples and original delta-debugging implementation.
limitations: Examples inspected, not executed; smaller failure is not automatically the original causal mechanism or globally minimal input.

title: Finding and Understanding Bugs in C Compilers
locator: §§1–2 generation semantics; §3.1 CompCert; §3.2 experiment design; PDF pp.1–3,6
claim: Differential compiler testing needs defined comparable semantics; verified portions and unverified boundaries require distinct claims.
context: Csmith generated C programs and historical GCC/LLVM/CompCert versions.
limitations: Original Utah URL timed out; author paper read through Stanford copy. Historical results do not describe present compiler quality.

title: An Empirical Analysis of Flaky Tests
locator: HBase case example PDF pp.3–4; §§2,5.2,6; PDF pp.9–10
claim: Flakiness can arise in tests or production code; condition synchronization and bounded timeouts differ from fixed sleeps.
context: Keyword-selected fixing commits across Apache projects.
limitations: Fixed cases and commit keywords bias recall; limited mobile/GUI coverage; human classification.

title: Flaky Tests at Google and How We Mitigate Them
locator: Main article paragraphs on reruns, three-failure policy, quarantine and false negatives
claim: Reruns and quarantine reduce immediate friction but delay or hide legitimate failures.
context: Google internal CI and test corpus in 2016.
limitations: Historical organizational observations, not a controlled intervention or universal flakiness rate.

title: Where do our flaky tests come from?
locator: Test size; objective RAM/binary buckets; tool versus size sections
claim: Resource size was associated with flakiness; tool correlations should not be mistaken for causes.
context: Mostly hermetic Google tests observed over a week.
limitations: Subjective size labels, bucket composition and organization-specific measurements; deleting large tests was not evaluated as a quality intervention.

title: Code Coverage Best Practices
locator: Main article bullets on lossy metric, edge cases, mutation, risk and no ideal coverage number
claim: Coverage identifies unexecuted areas but does not establish assertion adequacy; targets depend on criticality and context.
context: Google's experience with large-company testing initiatives.
limitations: Authors explicitly call causal defect reduction an open research question; suggested internal figures are not universal requirements.

title: Coverage Is Not Strongly Correlated with Test Suite Effectiveness
claim: Controlling suite size weakens coverage/effectiveness correlation; the study cannot establish causality.
context: 31,000 generated suites across five Java systems; mutation used as effectiveness proxy.
limitations: Equivalent-mutant approximation and project/test-selection assumptions constrain construct and external validity.

title: Rigorous Benchmarking in Reasonable Time
locator: §8.2 layout comparison, PDF pp.8–9 (zero-based7–8); §§9–11 repetition/effect-size intervals
claim: Repetition must reflect variation levels; smaller reference-case variation coexists with significant layout-dependent mean shifts.
context: Training P3/P4/P5 without LTO; reference P3 with LTO in randomized and baseline builds.
limitations: Input size alone is not isolated; confidence intervals do not eliminate uncontrolled bias.
version: 2013 accepted manuscript; repository notes corrected version

title: Producing Wrong Data Without Doing Anything Obviously Wrong!
claim: Environment/layout variation can bias a performance comparison; setup randomization and causal analysis expose some biases.
context: Older CPUs, compilers and SPEC CPU2006 C workloads, including training inputs.
limitations: Bias depends on workload/platform/build conditions; later comparisons do not isolate input size alone. Randomization over known factors cannot remove all unknown bias.

title: Details of the Cloudflare outage on July 2, 2019
locator: The events of July 2; How Cloudflare operates; What went wrong; remediation list
claim: Functional checks, deployment policy, resource protection and recovery dependencies all contributed to the reported failure chain.
context: WAF rule rollout and historical global CPU exhaustion.
limitations: Operator reconstruction; reported interventions inspected but not reproduced; announced remedies are not verified present behavior.

title: Postmortem of database outage of January 31
locator: Timeline; Broken recovery procedures; Recovering GitLab.com; root cause problem2; Improving recovery
claim: Backup production, notification delivery, snapshot semantics and restore performance were separate failed or incomplete contracts.
context: GitLab.com 2017 database deletion and recovery.
limitations: Historical operator report, no independent replay; cannot infer present backup/recovery state.

title: October 21 post-incident analysis
locator: Background; 23:13 recovery decision; technical and organizational initiatives
claim: Brief connectivity loss triggered divergent state and lengthy recovery; restoring connectivity alone did not restore service correctness.
context: October2018 MySQL failover and data reconciliation.
limitations: Historical reported causality and future plans, not reproduced or a statement about current architecture.

title: Monitoring Distributed Systems
locator: Symptoms Versus Causes; Black-Box Versus White-Box; Four Golden Signals; tail latency
claim: Symptoms, internal causes, response codes, and user-correct outputs require different observations.
context: SRE monitoring and alerting of user-facing distributed services.
limitations: Experience-based guidance; complexity and metric choices require system-specific interpretation.

title: Effective Troubleshooting
locator: Theory; Common Pitfalls; Triage/Examine/Diagnose; hypothesis testing
claim: Use system knowledge, competing explanations and observations or controlled treatments to narrow causes.
context: Operational diagnosis where mitigation may precede full explanation.
limitations: A general method does not replace knowing a system; safe experiment design remains contextual.

title: Alerting on SLOs
locator: Alerting Considerations; Multiwindow Multi-Burn-Rate; Low-Traffic Services; Extreme Availability Goals
claim: Alert quality depends on user impact, signal volume and detection/reset tradeoffs; synthetic traffic can hide real-user failures.
context: Request-based SLO/error-budget alerting.
limitations: Example thresholds and windows are starting points, not universal values; low-volume/high-value requests differ.

title: OWASP Application Security Verification Standard 5.0.0 requirements
locator: Version field; V1.1 canonicalization/output encoding; V1.2 context-specific injection requirements
claim: Security verification requirements are versioned and context-specific; controls must match the interpreter and boundary.
context: Modern web applications/services; selected control families inspected.
limitations: Not an audit or proof of product security; not every requirement examined; applicability and assurance scope need explicit selection.

title: Secure Software Development Framework Version1.1
locator: §1 introduction; PDF p.12 (printed p.3), risk/cost/applicability and shared responsibility
claim: SSDF explicitly rejects checklist application and calls for risk-based customization and ownership.
context: Secure development practices integrated with an organization's lifecycle.
limitations: Version1.1 inspected, not a claim it is latest; no organization assessed and no legal obligation inferred.

title: Threat Modeling Cheat Sheet
locator: Overview; System Modeling; Threat Identification; Response and Mitigations; Review and Validation
claim: Model the actual system and applicable threats, select responses, and validate; threat models need updating as systems change.
context: Adversarial application-security reasoning.
limitations: Guidance rather than empirical effectiveness measurement; no single methodology is declared universally correct.

title: The USE Method
locator: Intro; Summary; terminology and interpretation sections
claim: Start resource investigations with utilization, saturation and errors questions, rather than collecting convenient metrics.
context: Server/resource bottleneck triage.
limitations: Author presents it as one tool in a wider toolbox; claimed success percentages are personal experience, not controlled estimates.

title: Active Benchmarking
locator: Summary; Passive/Active Benchmarking; checklist
claim: Observe system components during the benchmark to identify what is actually limiting measured work.
context: Diagnosing benchmark validity and misleading bottlenecks.
limitations: Practitioner guidance, not a requirement for hours-long runs on every task; instrumentation may itself affect behavior.

title: Google Benchmark User Guide
locator: Random Interleaving; CPU/Manual Timers; Preventing Optimization; Reporting Statistics
claim: DoNotOptimize does not prevent all expression optimization; repetitions and timer selection change what results mean.
context: C++ microbenchmark harness.
limitations: Live documentation without pinned library revision; no benchmark executed or generated assembly inspected here.

title: How SQLite Is Tested
locator: §§3.3–3.4 crash/compound faults;4.1.6 fuzz/MC-DC tension;7.2 defensive macros;7.5 delivery-build rerun
claim: Coverage, fault injection, fuzzing and delivery-build tests establish different things; durable infrastructure justifies intensive verification.
context: Defined SQLite core/configuration and library durability.
limitations: Documented practices, not locally run tests; not all extensions/configurations covered by stated percentages; page's inventory figures include historical version references.

title: A Survey on Metamorphic Testing
locator: §§1–2, PDF pp.2–3; methods/challenges follow-up fetches timed out
claim: Relations between executions supply partial oracles with explicit input transformations and preconditions.
context: Survey covers119 papers from1998–2015; selected conceptual sections inspected.
limitations: Underlying119 studies not read; no comprehensive effectiveness conclusion drawn; later sections unavailable on follow-up.

title: FoundationDB: A Distributed Unbundled Transactional Key Value Store
locator: Simulation testing PDF pp.8–9; Limitations p.9; §6.2 p.11
claim: Deterministic simulation combines invariants, recoverability oracles and tuned faults, while excluding some performance and external dependency behavior.
context: FoundationDB's Flow-based simulated runtime and production system.
limitations: Authors' productivity/reliability reports are not controlled comparisons; model assumptions and real OS contracts can differ.

title: Redis-Raft1b3fbf6
evidence_type: original independent commissioned system testing report
locator: §2 Test Design;§3.19 history rewriting; result table; recommendations
claim: Reported anomalous histories can establish safety failures while underlying causes remain uncertain.

limitations: Historical selected builds/workloads, Redis-funded report; no generalization to other Redis replication products or present versions; no local replay.

context: Historical ASan implementation and its evaluation.
